Getting started / language

System and app languages

Switch system menus to English to match the screenshots. Keep Chinese in the language list so you can switch back later.

Specified operation verified · Peer review pending

Baseline: MA1 · Android 15 · MAG1WW53. Captured: 2026-10-14. This page is an editorial draft. Steps have not been tested except where explicitly stated.

Settings → System → Languages → System Languages

Before you start

  • Device unlocked
  • Screenshots use English (United States)
  • Changing the language may also affect regional formats and some app interfaces

Steps

  1. Open Settings, scroll to System, then open Languages and System Languages.

    View screenshot for this step ↗ View screenshot for this step ↗

  2. If English (United States) is already listed, press and hold its drag handle on the right and move it to position 1. Tapping the language name does not reorder it.

    View screenshot for this step ↗

  3. When asked “Change system language to English (United States)?”, select Change.
  4. If English is missing, select Add a language, choose English and a region, then drag it to position 1. Adding a new language has not been tested in this session.
  5. Return to Settings and check that headings such as Network & internet and Display are in English. Some app names may remain in Chinese even after a successful change.

    View screenshot for this step ↗

Buttons and options

Button / optionPurpose and limits
Preferred language orderThe system, apps and websites use the first language they support in the list
Add a languageAdds a language without necessarily making it the preferred language
ChangeConfirms the change to the system language and regional preferences
CancelCancels this change
App languagesSets a separate language for supported apps; availability varies by app
Labels observed on the device
  • Preferred Language
  • System Languages
  • App languages
  • Regional preferences
  • Speech
  • On-device recognition
  • Text-to-speech output
  • Your system, apps, and websites use the first supported language from your preferred languages.
  • Preferred language order
  • English (United States)
  • Simplified Chinese (China)
  • Traditional Chinese (Hong Kong)
  • To select a language for each app, go to app language settings.

A visible label confirms that an entry or option exists. It does not mean every listed action has been tested.

Expected result and recorded evidence

English (United States) was moved from position 2 to position 1, and the English Settings page was confirmed.

Verified scope: moved the existing English (United States) entry from position 2 to position 1, selected Change and checked English Settings.

Cancel, exit and restore

In the same list, move Simplified Chinese (China) back to position 1 and confirm Change. There is no need to delete English or Traditional Chinese.

Troubleshooting

  • Order unchanged: drag the handle on the right instead of tapping the language name
  • Some apps remain in Chinese: check App languages or the app’s own language setting; do not interrupt ongoing work unnecessarily
  • Menu not found: search Settings for “language” and check the system version

Limits and versions

MAG1WW53 / Android 15. Reordering and confirming the language were tested. Adding a language and changing individual app languages were not tested.

Device and packaging → Official MAG1 specifications

Before you start

  • Have the phone and packing list ready
  • Keep ports dry
  • Do not insert the SIM eject tool into a microphone opening

Steps

  1. Compare the package label—model MA1, product MAG1—with the order. Do not publish the IMEI or serial number.
  2. Identify the USB-C port, 3.5 mm headphone jack, SIM tray, cameras and side buttons. Their exact positions still require an annotated hardware check; do not insert an eject tool based on a guess.
  3. Check the packing list for the phone, cable, charger, SIM eject tool and any NFC accessories. A feature listed on the website does not mean its accessory is included in every shipment.
  4. Identify the power and volume buttons from the device markings. Short presses, long presses and button combinations each need verification on this model.
  5. Remove transport protection before first use. Check the glass, ports and accessories for damage; contact the seller if anything is damaged.

Buttons and options

Button / optionPurpose and limits
USB-CThe website specifies USB 2.0; the connector alone does not establish video-output support
Headphone jackThe website specifies 3.5 mm
SIMThe website specifies dual Nano-SIM and no eSIM support
ModelThe device reports MA1

Expected result and recorded evidence

The model matches the ADB information collected in this session. Package contents and button positions have not been physically verified.

Cancel, exit and restore

If accessories do not match, stop connecting them. Keep the packaging and order details and contact official support.

Troubleshooting

  • Eject tool does not fit: first confirm the SIM-tray opening; do not force it
  • Physical damage: stop charging and using the device, and retain evidence

Limits and versions

Website specifications are manufacturer information. No external-camera footage was captured; a screen recording cannot verify physical handling.

First boot and initial setup

Power on → Android setup wizard

Before you start

  • Sufficient battery charge and dry ports
  • A working network; your Google account if you choose account-based services, and the original credentials if ownership verification is requested
  • The current test device is already initialized; reproducing the wizard would require a reset

Steps

  1. Use the power button to start the phone. Follow the supplied instructions for how long to hold it; no unverified duration is specified here.
  2. Choose a language and region on the welcome screen, then follow the on-screen instructions.
  3. Connect to your own Wi-Fi or SIM data as prompted. Complete any network sign-in if required.
  4. Review account, data-transfer, service and permission choices. Copying data from an old phone is the user’s decision; Skip is not a mandatory choice.
  5. The owner should enter the screen lock directly on the device. Do not record or share the password.
  6. After reaching the home screen, check the system and bundled app versions, then follow the quick start for everyday settings.

Buttons and options

Button / optionPurpose and limits
Continue / NextUse only if shown on the current screen; the exact button requires verification on an uninitialized device
SkipWhether a step can be skipped depends on the actual screen
Account authenticationMust be completed by the device owner

Expected result and recorded evidence

The read-only audit records this phone as already set up. Its installed wizard contains account-skip and ownership-verification branches. A complete first-run or post-reset flow has not been reproduced; no successful setup video is claimed.

Cancel, exit and restore

Go back only where the wizard allows it. Do not factory-reset the device solely to recapture the wizard.

Troubleshooting

  • Network unavailable: try a known working connection
  • Old-device or account verification required: prepare the owner’s credentials; do not bypass device protection

Limits and versions

Baseline MAG1WW53 / Android 15; evidence dated 2026-10-14. Setup-wizard version 236.827749626 was examined as installed. Code paths are reference evidence, not a guarantee of the screen shown in every configuration. Retest after firmware or wizard updates on a suitable test unit; this review did not reset the phone.

Peer review: pending. Publication status: unpublished.

Three separate processes

ProcessMeaning and limits
Android initial setupLanguage, network and account choices before normal use. Completing setup does not establish a warranty date or node eligibility.
Factory reset protection (FRP)Ownership verification associated with a protected device after reset. It is separate from ordinary new-device account choices.
MAGNE device wallet bindingAn independent app-and-server binding flow. See the client-code reference below; it has not been executed in this review.

Device wallet binding: client-code reference →

Google account choices and reset protection

MAG1 uses a Google setup wizard. The installed version contains a path for skipping account setup. Follow the choices actually shown on your phone: the visible path depends on device state, configuration and later manufacturer checks. This is not proof that every first-boot scenario can skip an account, or that the flow is identical to a Pixel.

If reset protection requests ownership verification, use the original credentials required by the on-screen prompt. This phone’s current FRP state was not established by the read-only audit.

The available diagnostic query was blocked by system permissions. Missing settings or empty output do not prove protection is off. Ask the manufacturer for an official read-only status report if confirmation is needed; repeating USB authorization is not a solution to this restriction.

Wired charging, wireless charging and battery care

Recognize charging status and investigate heat or slow charging. A rated maximum does not mean every session reaches that power.

Baseline: MA1 · Android 15 · MAG1WW53. Captured: 2026-10-14. This page is an editorial draft. Steps have not been tested except where explicitly stated.

USB-C / compatible wireless charger → Settings → Battery

Before you start

  • Compatible, undamaged charger, cable or wireless charging pad
  • Dry device and ports
  • Remove metal objects and incompatible cases before wireless charging

Steps

  1. Wired: connect an undamaged cable to USB-C and a compatible charger, then check for the on-screen charging indicator.
  2. Wireless: align the center of the phone’s back as directed by the charging-pad instructions, keep it in contact and check for charging status. The alignment position has not been tested.
  3. Open Settings → Battery, note the charge level and status, then check later whether the charge level increases.
  4. Stop charging if there is overheating, an unusual smell, swelling, liquid ingress or port damage, and contact a qualified repair service.
  5. When finished, unplug by holding the connector rather than pulling the cable. Lift the phone off the pad to end wireless charging.

Buttons and options

Button / optionPurpose and limits
Battery percentageShows the battery percentage in the status bar
Battery usageShows battery use; it does not verify the charger’s rated output
Wired / wireless powerMeasurement equipment and recorded conditions are required to claim rated charging performance
Labels observed on the device

  • Battery Saver
  • Ultra saving mode
  • Adaptive Battery
  • Battery percentage
  • App battery settings
  • App standby optimizer
  • Stop app after screen lock
  • Auto launch management
  • Power intensive apps
  • Remaining battery life is approximate and can change based on usage

A visible label confirms that an entry or option exists. It does not mean every listed action has been tested.

Expected result and recorded evidence

A charging indicator should appear and the charge level should rise. Charging power and wireless charging were not measured in this session.

Cancel, exit and restore

Unplug the charger or remove the phone from the pad. Allow it to cool naturally if temperature is a concern.

Troubleshooting

  • No charging: try a known working outlet, cable and charger
  • Wireless charging fails: check alignment, metal objects and the case
  • Slow charging: check temperature, current workload and charger negotiation; the animation alone cannot diagnose a fault

Limits and versions

The official specifications checked on 2026-10-14 list 5000 mAh and up to 33 W wired / 15 W wireless charging. An older alpha PDF lists 5010 mAh and IP67, which conflict with the current public page; those older specifications are not used here.

Settings → Sound & vibration

Before you start

  • Device unlocked
  • Avoid testing sounds where quiet is required
  • Start headphones at a low volume

Steps

View this session's screenshots and videos ↓

  1. Open Sound & vibration and inspect the volume sliders shown on the device.
  2. Adjust the slider for the relevant source: Media volume for playback, Ring volume for incoming calls, or Alarm volume for alarms. Confirm the exact labels against the screenshot.

  4. Open Vibration & haptics to view call, notification and touch-feedback options. Do not assume support for options that are not shown.

Settings → Notifications → Do Not Disturb / Flash notifications

Before you start

  • Record the current exceptions and schedule rules
  • Use test contacts and test alerts
  • Do not test by calling a real emergency number

Steps

  1. Open Do Not Disturb from Notifications.
  2. Review allowed contacts, apps, alarms and schedules. Confirm the exact exception options on this device’s subpages.

  4. In Flash notifications, check camera-light and screen-flash options. Use a harmless test alert, and avoid testing close to anyone’s eyes.
  5. Afterward, check whether Do Not Disturb is still enabled so that missed alerts are not mistaken for a network problem.

Settings → Battery

Before you start

  • Record the original settings
  • Check the impact before changing settings for phone, messaging, authenticator or security apps
  • Remaining battery life is an estimate

Steps

  1. Open Battery and review charge level and Battery usage. Identify high-use sources before changing settings.
  2. Read Battery Saver and Ultra saving mode. Ultra saving may restrict available apps; it is not enabled on the user’s behalf in this session.
  3. Review Adaptive Battery; it is separate from restrictions applied to an individual app.
  4. Read the descriptions for App standby optimizer, Stop app after screen lock, Auto launch management and Power intensive apps.
  5. For delayed alerts, compare the app’s background permission, auto-start and stop-after-lock rules. Restore permission for a test app if needed.
  6. After a change, reproduce an alert with the same test app in foreground, background and locked states. Record battery level, network and elapsed time.

Device wallet binding: client-code reference

The installed device-binding app, version 1.2.15, was examined without running a binding operation. Its login path involves a security-chip PIN check; the inspected login and binding paths did not show a Google-account prerequisite. This is a limited code finding, not a guarantee for every service version.

  • The client accepts a wallet address in EVM format. Passing a format check does not verify control of that wallet.
  • The app reads a chip identifier, then requests a fresh challenge from the binding server for that device and address.
  • It signs the challenge-related data through the security chip and verifies the returned data locally.
  • It submits the binding data and signature. The client saves a binding result only after both the HTTP request and the business response succeed; it can later query the server’s current record.
  • No binding, signature or server request was executed. The actual service configuration and reachability, this phone’s binding state and the binding time remain unverified.
  • A displayed binding time can fall back to the phone’s clock when the server omits it. It is not automatically a server activation timestamp. A saved chip identifier also does not establish successful binding.
  • Client error branches cover an already-bound device or address. Server-side one-to-one rules, unbinding and changing the linked wallet still need official confirmation.
  • This client flow does not establish an on-chain registration, warranty start date, node qualification or reward entitlement.

Getting started / charging

Wired charging, wireless charging and battery care

Recognize charging status and investigate heat or slow charging. A rated maximum does not mean every session reaches that power.

Awaiting verification

Baseline: MA1 · Android 15 · MAG1WW53. Captured: 2026-10-14. This page is an editorial draft. Steps have not been tested except where explicitly stated.

USB-C / compatible wireless charger → Settings → Battery

Before you start

  • Compatible, undamaged charger, cable or wireless charging pad
  • Dry device and ports
  • Remove metal objects and incompatible cases before wireless charging

Steps

  1. Wired: connect an undamaged cable to USB-C and a compatible charger, then check for the on-screen charging indicator.
  2. Wireless: align the center of the phone’s back as directed by the charging-pad instructions, keep it in contact and check for charging status. The alignment position has not been tested.
  3. Open Settings → Battery, note the charge level and status, then check later whether the charge level increases.
  4. Stop charging if there is overheating, an unusual smell, swelling, liquid ingress or port damage, and contact a qualified repair service.
  5. When finished, unplug by holding the connector rather than pulling the cable. Lift the phone off the pad to end wireless charging.

Getting started / first-boot

First boot and initial setup

Set the language, network and account on a device that has not yet been initialized.

Static evidence available · First-run test pending

Baseline: MA1 · Android 15 · MAG1WW53. Captured: 2026-10-14. This page is an editorial draft. Steps have not been tested except where explicitly stated.

Power on → Android setup wizard

Before you start

  • Sufficient battery charge and dry ports
  • A working network; your Google account if you choose account-based services, and the original credentials if ownership verification is requested
  • The current test device is already initialized; reproducing the wizard would require a reset

Steps

  1. Use the power button to start the phone. Follow the supplied instructions for how long to hold it; no unverified duration is specified here.
  2. Choose a language and region on the welcome screen, then follow the on-screen instructions.
  3. Connect to your own Wi-Fi or SIM data as prompted. Complete any network sign-in if required.
  4. Review account, data-transfer, service and permission choices. Copying data from an old phone is the user’s decision; Skip is not a mandatory choice.
  5. The owner should enter the screen lock directly on the device. Do not record or share the password.
  6. After reaching the home screen, check the system and bundled app versions, then follow the quick start for everyday settings.

Buttons and options

Button / optionPurpose and limits
Continue / NextUse only if shown on the current screen; the exact button requires verification on an uninitialized device
SkipWhether a step can be skipped depends on the actual screen
Account authenticationMust be completed by the device owner

Expected result and recorded evidence

The read-only audit records this phone as already set up. Its installed wizard contains account-skip and ownership-verification branches. A complete first-run or post-reset flow has not been reproduced; no successful setup video is claimed.

Cancel, exit and restore

Go back only where the wizard allows it. Do not factory-reset the device solely to recapture the wizard.

Troubleshooting

  • Network unavailable: try a known working connection
  • Old-device or account verification required: prepare the owner’s credentials; do not bypass device protection

Limits and versions

Baseline MAG1WW53 / Android 15; evidence dated 2026-10-14. Setup-wizard version 236.827749626 was examined as installed. Code paths are reference evidence, not a guarantee of the screen shown in every configuration. Retest after firmware or wizard updates on a suitable test unit; this review did not reset the phone.

Peer review: pending. Publication status: unpublished.

Screenshots & videos

Suitable capture material is not yet available. No illustrations or screenshots from another model have been substituted.

Three separate processes

ProcessMeaning and limits
Android initial setupLanguage, network and account choices before normal use. Completing setup does not establish a warranty date or node eligibility.
Factory reset protection (FRP)Ownership verification associated with a protected device after reset. It is separate from ordinary new-device account choices.
MAGNE device wallet bindingAn independent app-and-server binding flow. See the client-code reference below; it has not been executed in this review.

Device wallet binding: client-code reference →

Google account choices and reset protection

MAG1 uses a Google setup wizard. The installed version contains a path for skipping account setup. Follow the choices actually shown on your phone: the visible path depends on device state, configuration and later manufacturer checks. This is not proof that every first-boot scenario can skip an account, or that the flow is identical to a Pixel.

If reset protection requests ownership verification, use the original credentials required by the on-screen prompt. This phone’s current FRP state was not established by the read-only audit.

The available diagnostic query was blocked by system permissions. Missing settings or empty output do not prove protection is off. Ask the manufacturer for an official read-only status report if confirmation is needed; repeating USB authorization is not a solution to this restriction.

Steps

  1. Compare the package label—model MA1, product MAG1—with the order. Do not publish the IMEI or serial number.
  2. Identify the USB-C port, 3.5 mm headphone jack, SIM tray, cameras and side buttons. Their exact positions still require an annotated hardware check; do not insert an eject tool based on a guess.

  4. Identify the power and volume buttons from the device markings. Short presses, long presses and button combinations each need verification on this model.

Baseline: MA1 · Android 15 · MAG1WW53. Captured: 2026-10-14. This page is an editorial draft. Steps have not been tested except where explicitly stated.

Settings → Network & internet → Hotspot & tethering

Before you start

  • A test network and a second test device
  • Confirm that the plan permits tethering and has sufficient data
  • Do not record or publish the hotspot password

Steps

View this session's screenshots and videos ↓

  1. Open Hotspot & tethering and check which sharing methods are actually shown.
  2. Wi-Fi hotspot: set a test name, strong password and an available band before enabling it. Do not infer 6 GHz or password-free support from an unopened subpage.
  3. On the second device, choose the test hotspot, enter the password and check a known working website.
  4. USB tethering: connect a data-capable cable to the computer and wait for detection before checking whether USB tethering is selectable. A charging-only cable cannot transfer data.
  5. Bluetooth tethering: pair the test device first, then enable the actual sharing switch. The receiving device must support it.
  6. Turn off all sharing switches enabled for the test immediately afterward.

Device wallet binding: client-code reference

The installed device-binding app, version 1.2.15, was examined without running a binding operation. Its login path involves a security-chip PIN check; the inspected login and binding paths did not show a Google-account prerequisite. This is a limited code finding, not a guarantee for every service version.

  • The client accepts a wallet address in EVM format. Passing a format check does not verify control of that wallet.
  • The app reads a chip identifier, then requests a fresh challenge from the binding server for that device and address.
  • It signs the challenge-related data through the security chip and verifies the returned data locally.
  • It submits the binding data and signature. The client saves a binding result only after both the HTTP request and the business response succeed; it can later query the server’s current record.
  • No binding, signature or server request was executed. The actual service configuration and reachability, this phone’s binding state and the binding time remain unverified.
  • A displayed binding time can fall back to the phone’s clock when the server omits it. It is not automatically a server activation timestamp. A saved chip identifier also does not establish successful binding.
  • Client error branches cover an already-bound device or address. Server-side one-to-one rules, unbinding and changing the linked wallet still need official confirmation.
  • This client flow does not establish an on-chain registration, warranty start date, node qualification or reward entitlement.

  • Do not record or display passwords, QR codes or real network names

Steps

  1. Open Network & internet → Internet. This entry was verified; nearby networks are excluded from the public captures.
  2. If Wi-Fi is off, use the actual switch and wait for the network list to refresh.

TROUBLESHOOTING / Diagnose an issue

Find the cause.
Change one thing.

Record the time, version, error message and reproduction steps. Stop before authentication, payment, deletion or reset. Clearing data should not be the first step.

SymptomFirst checksRelated steps
No internet connectionCheck airplane mode and Internet first, then SIM, VPN, DNS and captive-portal sign-in. Change one item at a time.Open guide →
Delayed notificationsCheck app notifications → channels → Do Not Disturb → Battery startup/lock-screen restrictions → network.Open guide →
Screen hard to read or turns off quicklyCheck brightness, adaptive brightness, Screen timeout and accessibility display options under Display.Open guide →
Unexpected sound or vibrationDistinguish media, calls, ringtones, notifications and alarms; check headphone output and Do Not Disturb.Open guide →
USB only chargesCheck the data cable, device unlock, USB purpose and computer recognition. A charging-only cable cannot transfer data.Open guide →
Bluetooth device not foundPut the accessory in pairing mode and check distance and identity. Cancel immediately if pairing codes differ.Open guide →
Insufficient storageInspect Storage categories first, then handle only content with verified backups. Do not clear wallet data.Open guide →
Wallet will not open or recovery failsPreserve data and check the package and version. Stop before confirmation if a test account or authentication is unavailable.Open guide →
Different system versionCompare the actual build and region and recheck entries. This review does not install updates or flash firmware.Open guide →
Liquid ingress, damage or abnormal heatStop use and charging and contact official support. Current specifications do not promise immersion protection.Open guide →

Before contacting support

  • Product model and build; app name, package and version.
  • Error text, time, network/accessory conditions and the shortest reproduction steps.
  • Screenshots without personal data; share necessary order details only through private official channels.
  • Do not send private keys, recovery phrases, passwords or verification codes, or publish personal identification.

The official Contact page lists official@magne.ai for product support. No external message was sent. Warranty duration and service terms await a formal policy.

MAGNE, AI and Web3 / Gemini

Gemini: side key, live screen sharing and webpage summaries

Open Gemini over a public webpage, share the screen in Live, or request a readable webpage summary.

Specified operations verified · Peer review pending

Verified on MAG1WW53: simulated power-key invocation, starting Live screen sharing, browsing the public MAG1 page, stopping sharing and ending Live; a separate Summarize page request produced an English response. Android media projection was checked both while active and after stopping. No spoken question or camera session was tested.

Press & hold power button → Gemini → Live / Summarize page

Gemini Live / Summarize page

Silent demonstration: microphone access is temporarily off, so the two Unblock microphone prompts are cancelled. Native touch markers, swipe trails and the coordinate strip are retained. The side-key press is simulated through ADB. No image masks or fabricated replies are used.

Before you start

  • An enabled Gemini app, Google as the digital assistant, an eligible signed-in account and a working network. Availability can differ by account, region and app version.
  • Use a public page. Close messages, account pages and sensitive notifications before sharing. The demonstration uses the MAG1 English product page.
  • Check Settings → System → Gestures → Press & hold power button → Digital assistant. This device already had Digital assistant selected; no change was needed.

Steps

  1. Open the MAG1 English product page in Chrome. Press and hold the side power button. Gemini appears over the page. The recording uses an ADB-simulated long press; it does not film a physical finger or test the physical button.
  2. For live sharing, select the Live icon at the lower right. This device also offers Share screen with Live. In the recorded route, the Live controls are opened first, then Screenshare.
  3. Read the Android sharing dialog. This recording uses Entire screen → Start. Anything visible while sharing may be sent to Google; do not switch to private content.
  4. Return to Chrome, scroll the public page, then tap the floating Gemini bubble to return to the Live controls. Tap Screenshare again to stop sharing, then the X button to end Live.
  5. For a text result, invoke Gemini over the public page again and select Summarize page. Wait for the English response, then scroll to read it. This sends the webpage context for a summary; it is a separate operation from continuous Live sharing.
  6. Compare the generated answer with the source page. The captured answer is an AI-generated summary of website claims, not independent validation of product specifications or capabilities.

Buttons and options

ControlPurpose
Digital assistantThe selected power-button long-press action on this device.
Share screen with Live / Live iconLive entry points observed in the assistant overlay. The recording uses the Live icon.
ScreenshareOpens Android consent; during sharing, tap again to stop.
MicrophoneMuted in the screen-sharing demonstration. Voice interaction was not evaluated.
Summarize pageRequests a text summary of the current public webpage.
X / End Live modeEnds the Live session.

Expected result and recorded evidence

Verified on MAG1WW53: simulated power-key invocation, starting Live screen sharing, browsing the public MAG1 page, stopping sharing and ending Live; a separate Summarize page request produced an English response. Android media projection was checked both while active and after stopping. No spoken question or camera session was tested.

Cancel, exit and restore

Stop Screenshare, end Live and dismiss the assistant. For this authorized test, Gemini was temporarily enabled and then restored to its original disabled state. Temporary touch-display settings, microphone access and the original captions setting were restored. Assistant defaults were checked against the original values. Existing conversation history and account data were not opened or deleted.

Troubleshooting

  • Power menu appears: check the long-press setting and the default digital assistant.
  • Gemini is disabled: open its App info and enable it only if you want to use it. This test device was restored to disabled after capture.
  • No Live, screen-sharing or summary entry: check app/account/region availability and current Google documentation; the same firmware alone does not guarantee identical cloud features.
  • Microphone warning in this recording: system microphone access was intentionally blocked, and Cancel kept it blocked. The Live microphone was also muted. These privacy prompts are part of the silent demo, not a Gemini failure.
  • The reply differs: model output and webpage content can change. Check the source rather than treating the recording as a fixed answer.

Limits and versions

Captured 2026-10-14 on MAG1WW53 / Android 15, with Gemini 1.0.795460806 and Google app 17.64.22.ve.arm64. The installed Gemini package has the Android SYSTEM flag on this unit; this does not establish the app state of every retail device. Recheck both firmware and Google/Gemini versions after updates. Cloud inference, physical-button reliability, voice quality, camera use, offline operation and connected personal services are outside this verification.

This is a feature demonstration, not a claim of Google endorsement or a test of every Gemini capability.

Sources and update checks

  • Google: Gemini Live
  • Google: Gemini Apps Privacy Hub
  • MAG1 English product page

Security and recovery / Private space

Private space: opening, unlocking and locking again

Find Private space on MAG1, recognise its unlocked state, and lock it again using the app drawer.

Launcher entry and manual locking verified

Verified on MAG1WW53: access to existing-space settings, fingerprint-authenticated opening, the unlocked launcher area, manual locking, and a fresh authentication request when reopening. Five device screenshots and three silent touch-trace videos are included below. The new unlock video shows entry and success, with an editorial note over the protected authentication interval.

Settings → Security & privacy → Private space

Before you start

  • An existing Private space was used on MAG1WW53. This is not a first-time setup demonstration.
  • Complete fingerprint authentication directly on the phone. Android protects the prompt from screen recording; the video labels that interval with an editorial note.
  • The captured system interface is English. App names may retain their own language. Only app icons are shown; no private app is opened.

Observed entry and locking steps

  1. From the Home screen, swipe up to open the app drawer, then scroll to the bottom to find Private. This route was observed with com.android.launcher3, version 15.
  2. Tap Private. When locked, this MAG1 displays Verify it’s you, Touch the fingerprint sensor and Use PIN. Complete authentication on the phone.
  3. In the new unlock recording, the owner completes fingerprint verification on the phone and the Private app list expands. The protected prompt itself records as black; explanatory text marks that interval.
  4. To finish, tap Lock in the Private header. The recorded test shows the private app area collapse and the header return to a padlock. Ordinary apps remain visible.
  5. Tap the locked Private entry to open it again. A fresh authentication request was confirmed outside recording, then cancelled; the space was left locked.
  6. To inspect its controls, open Settings → Security & privacy → Private space and authenticate. View the automatic-lock and hide pages without changing their current values.

Finding a hidden space: on-device instructions, not yet tested

The MAG1 hide-options page says that a hidden private space can be found by entering "private space" in the search bar, selecting Private space and unlocking it. This instruction was read on the phone; the hide switch remained Off, so hidden-space search has not been tested. Google’s reference is linked below for context.

Google Android Help: Private space

Controls and verification status

  • Private / Lock — App-drawer entry observed; manual locking recorded and re-entry authentication checked.
  • Private space lock — PIN displayed in Settings; credentials were not changed.
  • Lock private space automatically — Every time device locks selected. Also observed: 5 minutes after screen timeout; Only after device restarts. No policy change or timed test.
  • Hide private space when it’s locked — Off. The settings page and its search instructions were captured; hiding was not enabled.

Observed result

Verified on MAG1WW53: access to existing-space settings, fingerprint-authenticated opening, the unlocked launcher area, manual locking, and a fresh authentication request when reopening. Five device screenshots and three silent touch-trace videos are included below. The new unlock video shows entry and success, with an editorial note over the protected authentication interval.

Exit and restoration

The test ended with Private space locked and its authentication prompt cancelled. The hide switch stayed Off and automatic locking stayed Every time device locks. Touch indicators were restored to their original Off state. No space, credential, account or private app data was created, deleted or changed.

Troubleshooting

  • Unlocking the phone does not necessarily authenticate entry to Private space. Complete the additional prompt on the device.
  • Home returns to the ordinary launcher; use the Private header’s Lock button when you want to lock the space explicitly.
  • The fingerprint prompt is visible on the phone but records as black through ADB. The unlock video explains that interval; it does not recreate the system dialog.
  • If Private is missing, check its hide setting and your launcher version. The hidden-space search instructions were observed, but that route still needs a separate test.

Limits and firmware changes

Test baseline: MAG1WW53 / Android 15 / com.android.launcher3 version 15, 2026-10-14. Verified scope is limited to the routes and manual lock described above. Initial setup, private-app use, timed automatic locking and enabling hide were not tested. The relationship to MAGNE Web3 Secure Space and any vendor-specific shortcut remains unverified. Recheck after firmware or launcher updates.

Google notes that locked private-space apps stop running, and deleting the space removes its local apps and data. Do not use deletion as an ordinary exit step. Google Android Help: Private space

Screenshots & videos

English system interface in the white MAG1 frame. App icons and names remain as installed, without masking or renaming. Notification icons were hidden before capture. The new unlock clip includes entry and the successful return to the app list; Android blocks recording of the fingerprint prompt, so that interval carries an editorial note. All three videos are silent. The separate Lock clip begins with the space already unlocked.

Security and recovery / find-hub

Find Hub: finding and protecting a lost phone

Find the MAG1 device-finding settings and understand what has been checked before relying on remote recovery.

Entry and settings checked · Remote operations pending

MAG1WW53 · Android 15 · 2026-10-14

Settings → Security & privacy → Device finders → Find Hub

Before you start

  • For account-based Find Hub recovery, use the Google Account associated with the phone and keep a way to complete account verification from another device.
  • Check Location and Allow device to be located before the phone is lost. See Google’s preparation reference below.
  • For any demonstration, keep account details, maps, coordinates and other devices out of public captures.

Steps checked on this phone

  1. Open Settings → Security & privacy → Device finders. The inspected MAG1 showed Find Hub with the summary On.
  2. Open Find Hub and inspect Allow device to be located. It was enabled during this review; no switch was changed.
  3. Open Remote Lock to inspect its separate setting. Use Remote Lock was Off on this device. Return without changing it if you are only reviewing the configuration.
  4. The Find Hub settings page provides Find Hub app and Find Hub web entries. Their presence was confirmed; this review did not open an account device list or map.

Buttons and current settings

OptionObserved state and limits
Allow device to be locatedOn when inspected. This is a setting observation, not proof of a successful remote location request.
System LocationEnabled when checked through ADB. Position accuracy was not tested.
Remote Lock / Use Remote LockOff when inspected. The page describes phone-number-based remote screen locking; this is a separate option from the main Find Hub switch.
Find Hub app / Find Hub webBoth entries were visible. Account access and remote commands were not exercised.
Offline / powered-off findingNo offline-finding option appeared on the settings page inspected. This does not establish either support or lack of support; both capabilities remain unverified on MAG1.

If your phone is missing — service reference

The following is general Google guidance, not a recorded MAG1 test.

  1. On another device, open Find Hub, sign in to the phone’s Google Account and select the correct phone. Complete any requested identity check.
  2. Review the displayed location and its timestamp. Use Play sound for a nearby phone, or Mark as lost to lock it and provide return details. Availability depends on the service and device state.
  3. Factory reset permanently removes device data and ends further finding through Find Hub; an SD card may not be erased. Treat it as a last resort, not a routine test.

Google: Find, secure, or erase a lost Android device ↗

What was verified

Read-only checks on 14 October 2026 confirmed the settings route, Find Hub On, Allow device to be located On, system Location enabled and Remote Lock Off. No remote request was executed.

Exit and restore

Use Back to return from Remote Lock to Find Hub. This inspection changed no switches, accounts or permissions and sent no remote command.

Troubleshooting

  • If the phone is absent from the service, check the associated Google Account and follow Google’s preparation checklist. An installed app alone does not establish successful registration.
  • Do not interpret an old or unavailable location as a live position. Check the displayed time and connectivity.
  • If menus differ, record the firmware, Find Hub and Google Play services versions before comparing instructions.

Limits and versions

Baseline: MAG1WW53 / Android 15, 14 October 2026. Find Hub 3.1.763-04 is an updated system app; a factory copy 3.1.337-2 is present. Google Play services was 26.37.37. Location, ringing, lost mode, remote locking, erase, offline finding and powered-off finding were not tested. Recheck this chapter after firmware or Google component updates.

Evidence

Evidence consists of the read-only ADB package inventory and settings-page labels. No public screenshots or video have been added for this chapter; no account map or device list was captured.

References and related chapters

Google: Be ready to find a lost Android device ↗

See also: location settings and reset / account protection. Location · Setup / FRP

Additional coverage · 14 October 2026

Related chapters: Theft protection and automatic locking · Unknown tracker alerts and manual scanning
